newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission approves daily wheat export tax.
newsitem.headline: Commission approves daily wheat export tax.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday approved taxes of 15 ecus a tonne on daily exports of soft wheat grain and 20 ecus a tonne on wheat flour, Commission officials said.
"It's gone through," an official said, referring to a decision by the EU's 20 commissioners at a weekly meeting held this week in Strasbourg, France, because the European Parliament was in session.

The tax had been delayed a week after French EU Commissioner Edith Cresson objected, saying it was unnecessary because wheat prices were now falling and there was no longer a danger of EU wheat flooding abroad, attracted by higher world prices.
Previously unanimity was required because the proposal had been submitted under the so-called written procedure.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler this week resubmitted the proposal under a new procedure requiring only a simple majority vote which was taken after Cresson stated her objections.
Trade sources said that the week's delay had enabled nearly all exporters with special "nil-value" export licences to customs clear their grain and avoid paying the tax.
The export tax was a precautionary measure to avoid an overheating of the EU cereals market, Fischler said in a statement after the decision.
"The introduction of this tax is necessary to stabilise wheat prices," he said.
In recent weeks, prices have been increasing due to a generally low level of world stocks and uncertainty about EU and world harvests caused by climatic factors, Fischler said.
He added that the European Commission was responsible for preventing prices rising too high as well as preventing them falling too low.
